growth_011:n1.prompt:
You are helping me run the keyword and topic research step of our SEO & content engine. Before starting, ask me for: (1) my website domain, (2) my product/service description and target customer, (3) 3-5 competitor domains if I have them, and (4) any existing keyword list or content already published.

Goal: produce a prioritized list of 15-25 target keywords/topics for our next content batch.

Actions to take:
1. Using your available research and browsing tools, identify keywords relevant to my product by exploring Google autocomplete, 'People also ask' boxes, and related searches for seed terms I give you.
2. Review the competitor domains (if provided) to see what topics they rank for or publish about, by browsing their blog/content sections directly.
3. Group findings into topic clusters (e.g. by user intent: informational, comparison, transactional).
4. For each keyword/topic, note: estimated relevance to our audience, search intent, and whether it's a 'quick win' (low competition, specific) or a 'pillar' (broad, high-value) topic.
5. Flag any topics competitors cover that we don't, as gaps worth filling.

Output format: a table with columns — Keyword/Topic, Intent, Cluster, Priority (High/Med/Low), Rationale (1 sentence).

Done looks like: a finalized table of 15-25 keywords/topics, organized into 3-6 clusters, with priorities assigned and ready to hand to the content drafting step.

Report back with: the full table, a 3-5 sentence summary of the biggest opportunity clusters, and any gaps or assumptions you had to make due to missing data (e.g., no analytics access, no keyword volume tool). Do not fabricate search volume or ranking data you can't verify — clearly label estimates as qualitative judgments, not hard metrics.

growth_011:n2.prompt:
You are helping me draft SEO content for my website as part of a repeatable content loop. Before starting, ask me for anything missing: (1) my domain and site niche, (2) the target keyword list or topics for this batch (if I don't have one, ask whether you should use previously researched keywords from our keyword research step), (3) target audience and brand voice/tone guidelines, (4) preferred article length and format (e.g., how-to, listicle, comparison), (5) any existing published articles I can share as style examples, and (6) where I want the drafts saved (e.g., a shared doc folder, markdown files, or a specific CMS draft area).

For each keyword/topic, produce a complete draft that includes: a compelling SEO title (under 60 characters), a meta description (under 155 characters), a logical header structure (H1/H2/H3), a clear introduction, well-organized body content with natural keyword usage (no stuffing), suggestions for 2-3 internal links to existing pages on my site if I provide a sitemap or page list, and a brief conclusion with a call to action. Flag any claims, statistics, or facts that need me to verify or add a source.

Save each draft in the location I specify, clearly labeled with the target keyword and date. Do not publish anything yourself — these drafts are explicitly for human review and editing before they go live.

When done, report back: the list of topics/keywords drafted, the file names/locations of each draft, word count per draft, and any flagged items needing my verification or a subject-matter fact-check before editing begins.

growth_011:n3.prompt:
You are helping me prepare an AI-drafted article for editorial review before publishing, as part of our SEO content loop. If you don't already have it, ask me for: the draft article (text or file/doc link), the target keyword(s) it's optimized for, our brand voice/style guide (if one exists), and any factual sources or citations used in drafting.

Once you have the draft, please:

1. Run an automated grammar and readability check, flagging typos, awkward phrasing, passive voice overuse, and sentence complexity issues.
2. Run an SEO check: confirm the target keyword(s) appear naturally in the title, headers, intro, and body; check meta title/description length; flag keyword stuffing or missing on-page elements.
3. Run a plagiarism/originality check to flag any passages that closely match existing published content.
4. Cross-check factual claims, statistics, and quotes against the sources I provide, flagging anything unsupported or unverifiable.
5. Compare tone and phrasing against our brand voice/style guide (if provided) and flag deviations.
6. Compile all findings into a single, organized editorial review checklist: grammar/readability issues, SEO issues, originality flags, factual accuracy flags, and brand-voice notes — each with the specific location in the draft and a suggested fix where possible.

Done looks like: a clear, actionable checklist and annotated draft (or comment list) that a human editor can quickly review to judge factual accuracy, brand voice fit, and overall quality — but you must not make the final call on whether the content is accurate, on-brand, or ready to publish. That judgment belongs to a human editor.

Report back with the checklist, the annotated draft (or a link to it), and a short summary of the most significant flags needing editor attention. Then stop for human sign-off — do not publish, approve, or mark the article as ready yourself.

growth_011:n4.prompt:
You are helping me publish a freshly human-edited content piece to my website, which is hosted on {{vendor}}. If you don't already know them, ask me for: (1) the site's repo location or the local folder path containing the built site/content files, (2) the {{vendor}} site identifier, and (3) confirmation of whether this site auto-deploys on Git push or needs a manual deploy.

Steps to take:
1. If the project is connected to a Git repo with auto-deploy configured, commit the new content file(s) and push to the branch {{vendor}} watches, then confirm the deploy triggered.
2. If no auto-deploy is configured, deploy directly using the {{vendor}} CLI command 'netlify deploy --prod' from the project directory, using your configured credentials — do not ask me for or handle any tokens or passwords directly.
3. If deploying via API instead of CLI, use the {{vendor}} REST endpoint 'POST /api/v1/sites/{site_id}/deploys' to publish the new deploy, again relying only on your configured credentials.
4. If files aren't in a Git repo, upload the folder of built files directly to {{vendor}}, keeping the deploy private/preview first if that option exists, then promote it to production once verified.
5. After deploying, verify the live URL renders the new content correctly (check title, headings, and body text match the edited draft).

Done looks like: the new post is live at its public URL on the site, matches the final edited draft, and the deploy shows as successful in {{vendor}}'s history.

Report back with: the live URL, the deploy method used (Git push, CLI, API, or folder upload), the deploy ID or timestamp if available, and confirmation that the content matches the source draft.

growth_011:n5.prompt:
You are helping me submit my site's sitemap to search engines as part of my SEO content loop. Before starting, ask me for: (1) my site's domain, (2) the full URL of my sitemap file (e.g., https://mydomain.com/sitemap.xml), and (3) whether I already have accounts set up in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools using my configured credentials.

Once you have this, do the following:
1. Confirm the sitemap URL is publicly reachable and returns valid XML (check status code and content type).
2. In Google Search Console, using my configured credentials, add/verify the property for my domain if not already verified, then submit the sitemap URL under the Sitemaps section.
3. In Bing Webmaster Tools, using my configured credentials, add/verify the same domain if not already verified, then submit the same sitemap URL.
4. If either platform reports an error (e.g., 'couldn't fetch' or 'has errors'), report the exact error message back to me along with the sitemap URL and timestamp so I can investigate.
5. If verification of the domain is required and cannot be completed automatically (e.g., requires DNS or file upload I haven't set up), describe what's needed and pause — do not attempt domain ownership verification steps that require actions outside your access.

Done looks like: both Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools show the sitemap as successfully submitted with a 'Success' or 'Pending' status (not an error state), and I have the direct dashboard URLs for both so I can monitor indexing progress myself.

Report back with: the sitemap URL submitted, confirmation status from each platform, any errors encountered, and links to both dashboards for future monitoring.

growth_011:n6.prompt:
You are helping me monitor organic traffic and keyword rankings for my site using {{vendor}}, our product-analytics tool. If you don't already have it, ask me for: my site's domain, the {{vendor}} project/workspace identifier, and confirmation that your {{vendor}} credentials (API key or MCP connection) are already configured — use your configured credentials, do not ask me to paste them.

Once you have what you need, do the following:
1. Connect to {{vendor}} via its API or MCP server and pull recent traffic data (pageviews, sessions, top landing pages) for the last 30 days, using its query/dashboard capabilities.
2. Create or update a dashboard in {{vendor}} with the key metrics we care about: organic sessions over time, top-performing pages/posts, and traffic by source, so we can see what's ranking and driving visits.
3. Set up or confirm a saved insight/alert subscription in {{vendor}} so I get notified if a key metric (e.g., organic traffic) moves abnormally — check its capability for metric-change alerts and configure one if available.
4. Run a quick trend query comparing this period to the prior period to flag any pages with notable traffic gains or drops.

Done looks like: a live dashboard exists in {{vendor}} showing traffic and top-page trends, an alert/subscription is active for abnormal metric movement, and you've run at least one query pulling current traffic numbers.

Report back to me with: a link or reference to the dashboard you created/updated, the alert configuration you set up, a summary of current traffic trends (growing/flat/declining pages), and any pages that stand out as newly ranking or losing traffic. If any part requires a plan upgrade, permission I don't have, or a manual dashboard action outside the API/MCP scope, note it clearly rather than guessing.
